hints.content:
###The strategy

The perimeter of a pentagon is the sum of the lengths of all the sides. 

Note that $AB=EA$ and $BC=DE$, so we only need to find the lengths of $\overline{AB}$, $\overline{BC}$, and $\overline{CD}$.

Side $\overline{CD}$ is perfectly horizontal, so we can find its length using the $x$-coordinates of its endpoints.

We can find the length of $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{BC}$ using the Pythagorean theorem (or the distance formula).

###Step 1: Finding the length $AB$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} AB^2&= {\redE{6}^2 +\redE{7}^2 } &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
AB&= \sqrt{\redE{6}^2 +\redE{7}^2 } &&\text{Square root both sides}\\\\
&=\tealE{\sqrt{85}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Pentagon A B C D E has point A at zero, seven, point B at six, zero, point C at three, negative four, point D at negative three, negative four, and point E negative six, zero. Sides B C and D E are congruent. Sides A B and A E are congruent. A horizontal highlighted line of six units connects from point A to a vertical highlighted line of seven units to point B.

hints.content:
###Step 2: Finding the length $BC$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
BC^2&= \redE{3}^2 +\redE{4}^2  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
BC&= \sqrt{\redE{3}^2 +\redE{4}^2 }   &&\text{Square root both sides} \\\\
&=\sqrt{25} \\\\
&=\goldE{5}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Pentagon A B C D E has point A at zero, seven, point B at six, zero, point C at three, negative four, point D at negative three, negative four, and point E negative six, zero. Sides B C and D E are congruent. Sides A B and A E are congruent. A horizontal highlighted line of three units connects from point C to a vertical highlighted line of four units to point B.

hints.content:
###The answer

The exact perimeter of pentagon $ABCDE$ is $16+2\sqrt{85}$ units (approximately $34.4$ units).
